A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CryoSplat and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched reliably despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstructions on four real cryo-EM datasets, including FSC comparisons, Gaussian-count and anisotropy ablations, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains original reconstruction results and adds synthetic-noise experiments, corrected-FSC analysis, capacity studies, and initialization experiments.

M1.justification: v4 describes an optional optimization variant that splits all Gaussians at epoch boundaries (Appendix C.1, Algorithm 1), absent from v2's described procedure. The normalized anisotropic representation, projection, CTF modulation, FFT alignment, and MSE optimization remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that densification was used in the main experiments.

E1.justification: The four real datasets and known-pose homogeneous reconstruction task are retained. v4 adds a synthetic 80S ribosome scenario with known ground truth, uniformly sampled orientations, centered images, and controlled noise levels. This extends coverage to controlled simulated imaging conditions within the existing application.

E2.justification: For reconstruction-quality comparisons in Figures 2–3, v4 replaces cryoDRGN's backprojection implementation with cryoSPARC's Homogeneous Reconstruction Only job. The neural cryoDRGN comparator remains. The original backprojection implementation is retained for runtime and memory comparisons, making this a targeted comparator replacement.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce ground-truth FSC, masking and phase-randomization-corrected FSC, and decay-factor comparisons at gamma 0.1, 0.2, and 0.5. Capacity testing expands to 64–1,024 and 32,768–524,288 Gaussians; the high-count study uses 10 epochs and gamma 0.5. These are additional protocols; the main experiment's five-epoch, gamma-0.1 setting is retained.

E4.justification: v2 already examines Gaussian count, anisotropy, runtime, and memory. v4 retains those analyses and adds controlled SNR robustness, FSC-bias and masking checks, extreme-capacity failure analysis, an alpha-helix comparison with atomic-model overlay, and seed/spatial-initialization sensitivity tests (Appendix D.3–D.7). These substantially broaden the questions tested.

E5.justification: v2 provides no explicit repeated-seed uncertainty reporting. v4 Figure 13 reports mean FSC and a minimum–maximum envelope across ten seeds, 0–9, for EMPIAR-10049 with 2,048 Gaussians. This adds statistical reporting for one stability experiment, without extending uncertainty estimates to the main benchmark comparisons.

E6.justification: Figure 2 retains CryoSplat's reported resolutions of 3.80, 2.49, 3.30, and 4.26 Å. Voxel-baseline results are replaced, including RAG's 4.00 Å for v2 backprojection versus 4.23 Å for v4 cryoSPARC; this is not a same-method regression. Figures 8–14 add substantial findings on noise tolerance, FSC overestimation, extreme-count behavior, atomic detail, and initialization stability.

T1.justification: v4 adds explicit backward-pass derivations for normalized splatting (Equations 16–21), changes the transformed mean from Wμ+t to W(μ−t), and corrects the isotropic normalization denominator from sigma to sigma cubed. These exceed notation changes. However, new Equation 18 uses W where the stated forward transformation implies W transpose for column-gradient backpropagation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim reconstruction from randomly initialized GMMs under known poses without external consensus volumes, physically grounded projection, efficient CUDA implementation, and superior reconstruction quality over representative baselines. v4 expands the wording and implementation attribution but retains these central scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 largely interprets higher half-map FSC as better structural resolution. v4 Appendix D.4 explains that GMM self-consistency and low-pass behavior can inflate FSC, acknowledges overestimation under the default setting, and emphasizes qualitative assessment. It also adds limitations concerning high-count computational cost, low-count failure, and a symmetry-induced interpretation of RAG pose ambiguity.

D1.justification: v4 adds optimization/rasterization pseudocode, 16×16 tile and sorting details, synthetic-data generation instructions, and disclosure that baselines use spherical masking while CryoSplat uses unmasked FSC. It specifies a planned code-repository address without establishing release. Conversely, it drops v2 Table S1's explicit exclusions of voxelization and FSC-related half-map reconstruction from memory measurements.

R1.justification: v4 adds Ducrocq et al. (2024) and Shekarforoush et al. (2025) to GMM-related work, and Chen et al. (2013) for corrected FSC. The broader positioning against externally initialized GMM methods and photorealistic Gaussian splatting remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the document: FSC definitions and initialization/learning-rate explanations move into the main experimental section, while Fourier-space material and computational derivations move into a method appendix. It introduces a deeper numbered subsection hierarchy, expands the abstract and conclusion, and distinguishes observed Y from predicted X throughout the formulation.

P2.justification: v4 changes the two-column preprint into a single-column conference layout, rearranges comparison legends and panels, and promotes Table S1 to main-text Table 1. It adds a rasterization diagram, algorithm blocks, and multiple diagnostic figures. Earlier Figures S1 and S2 are retained as Figures 7 and 6, respectively.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens validation through ground-truth noise tests, repeated initializations, and capacity/atomic-detail analyses. Appendix D.4 investigates an important weakness left unexamined in v2: optimistic FSC-derived resolution estimates. Expanded computational documentation also improves inspectability. These gains remain qualified: the headline resolution-superiority claims are not fully reconciled with the default-setting FSC caveat, and new Equation 18 contains a rotation-transpose inconsistency.
